task: Diagnose the Phase 25.4 compiler performance gate failure in make check.
observation: The performance regression job ran concurrently with the rest of the parallel regression suite and measured wall-clock latencies up to roughly twice its limits. Running the same gate by itself passed all ten workloads, indicating scheduler contention rather than a compiler performance regression.
impact: The parallel test schedule produced false performance failures and obscured whether compiler behavior had regressed.
evidence: make --jobs="$(nproc)" check failure output supplied for check_phase25_4_performance_baseline

resolution.summary: The regression gate now runs exclusively after other parallel jobs drain; its standalone run passed all ten workloads.

suggestion: Keep wall-clock performance gates isolated from concurrent CPU-bound tests.
